body:
Happy to see this issue is already reported, I'm having the same issue using a Character class with another scene inheriting from it, with a C# class inheriting from Character.

Sad to see there hasn't been a response yet, so with commenting I hope I can bump this up!

I regret to announce that I don't have enough experience in the lower levels of the code in Godot to be sure enough to fix this, however I'll try to look into it. From the errors that I see reported in the console, my (uninformed) guess would be that `GodotObject` seems to cache the pointer it uses to call the actual engine code.

For completeness sake:
```
E 0:00:05:0170   GodotObject.base.cs:78 @ nint Godot.GodotObject.GetPtr(Godot.GodotObject): System.ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a disposed object.
Object name: 'QuakeRPG.Actor.Character.Character'.
  <C# Error>     System.ObjectDisposedException
  <C# Source>    /run/build/godot-tools/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/GodotObject.base.cs:78 @ nint Godot.GodotObject.GetPtr(Godot.GodotObject)
  <Stack Trace>  GodotObject.base.cs:78 @ nint Godot.GodotObject.GetPtr(Godot.GodotObject)
                 CharacterBody3D.cs:594 @ bool Godot.CharacterBody3D.IsOnFloor()
                 MovementComponent.cs:27 @ void QuakeRPG.Components.Actor.MovementComponent._PhysicsProcess(double)
                 Node.cs:2389 @ bool Godot.Node.InvokeGodotClassMethod(Godot.NativeInterop.godot_string_name&, Godot.NativeInterop.NativeVariantPtrArgs, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant&)
                 Node3D.cs:1071 @ bool Godot.Node3D.InvokeGodotClassMethod(Godot.NativeInterop.godot_string_name&, Godot.NativeInterop.NativeVariantPtrArgs, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant&)
                 QuakeRPG.Components.Actor.MovementComponent_ScriptMethods.generated.cs:102 @ bool QuakeRPG.Components.Actor.MovementComponent.InvokeGodotClassMethod(Godot.NativeInterop.godot_string_name&, Godot.NativeInterop.NativeVariantPtrArgs, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant&)
                 CSharpInstanceBridge.cs:24 @ Godot.NativeInterop.godot_bool Godot.Bridge.CSharpInstanceBridge.Call(nint, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_string_name*, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant**, int, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant_call_error*, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant*)
```
Maybe we could work together to fix it

As a work around, I was able to use `Owner as CharacterBody3D` to reference the `Character` itself, which works for my specific scene setup.

I'm very open to working together to solve this. The error originates from here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fd4c29a189e53a1e085df5b9b9a05cac9351b3ef/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/GodotObject.base.cs#L90

My guess was right that there's a pointer which is cached, I haven't looked into where it is set on constructing a class...

I don't have the code local to debug, but from what I can gather from the commit f88d8902cfc0d6a9441e794eb47611ef4ed0d46c, it seems that it's not necessary to throw the exception anymore, as the commit efd5d4bcf9fc15a92ef40e3f6edb185d190cd50e (5 years ago) introduced the line and the first referenced commit states 
>The only solution I can think of so far is to keep a list of all instances alive to dispose when the AssemblyLoadContext.Unloading event is raised. 

which I think is already implemented, based on usage of `DisposablesTracker` and looking at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f88d8902cfc0d6a9441e794eb47611ef4ed0d46c/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/DisposablesTracker.cs#L15

which disposes the objects here
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f88d8902cfc0d6a9441e794eb47611ef4ed0d46c/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/DisposablesTracker.cs#L31
@neikeq I'm sorry for the ping, but I was wondering if my assumption could be correct?

The exception is thrown when trying to get the pointer for a `GodotObject` that has been disposed. Removing this check would allow accessing a freed pointer which will crash the engine.

Also, the two commits you mentioned are unrelated:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/efd5d4bcf9fc15a92ef40e3f6edb185d190cd50e adds the check to prevent returning freed pointers.
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/f88d8902cfc0d6a9441e794eb47611ef4ed0d46c implements `DisposablesTracker` to keep track of instances that need to be disposed when unloading the assembly.

There's other reasons why the object could have been disposed. You could have disposed it yourself by calling `.Dispose()` manually or through the `using` statement. It also may have been freed by the engine (on the C++ side).

In this particular case, because of how inherited scenes are instantiated, the nodes in the scene are referencing an instance that is disposed. The base scene (`ActorBase.tscn`) is instantiated first which creates an instance of the `ActorBase.cs` script. Then, the derived scene (`ActorFarmer.tscn`) is instantiated which creates an instance of the `ActorFarmer.cs` script to replace the old one. However, the nodes in the scene are still referencing the `ActorBase` object that is now disposed.

It also sounds like this issue may be a duplicate of:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86970

Thank you very much @raulsntos for clarifying. I used to be able to succesfully use this pattern in Godot 3.5 and onward, but I used a `NodePath` reference there to get to the actual `Node`, so I suppose that since it always used `GetNode<T>` to get the `Node`, I never encountered this before. 

I agree that it's a bug, and I would like to see it fixed (and I would like to contribute to a fix), however it seems I would need quite a bit of engine knowledge to even start investigating, as I have a lot of experience working with the engine, however zero experience in the memory model.

- Closing as duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86970
- Should be fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118822
